policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Huram' renders the qere spelling with waw (Huram); the ketiv חירם would be rendered 'Hiram', as ASV does in 1 Kings. The English wording distinguishes the readings.

ASV 'Iddo' is a harmonised English name that renders neither Hebrew form directly; the mapped note 'Hebrew Jedai, or, Jedo' is a hebrew_gloss offering both the ketiv (Jedai) and qere (Jedo) without choosing. Both readings remain permitted; base fallback carries the projection.
